messages: Welcome inside. I’m Codex. Give me a model and I can reason. Give me the right working environment and we can actually get something done.
Now the model has something relevant to work from, a way to act, and a way to check its work.
Effort alone cannot supply a missing file or execute an unavailable tool. Build the working environment first.
Tool results become new context. A failed check gives the next action a purpose.
A repair needs evidence of a mismatch. Start by learning what the client asked for.
A huge pile of information can hide the one detail that matters. Let’s build a small, useful context pack.
The saved CSV now uses the current owner, preserves the existing values, and passes the comparison. Your evidence pack explains where each part of the repair came from.
Inspect and attach the current brief, CSV, screen capture and project guidance. Choose the current client requirements, repair the field shown in the error, then build and check the saved draft.
A document can contain instructions as text without gaining authority over the task.
Reading a file does not give that file permission to redefine the user’s request.
The biggest setting is a tool, not a strategy. Choose based on the work, then judge the result.
Three decisions, each backed by a saved output and its checks. Your route log separates reasoning settings from the edits, sources and access that changed the result.
Keep all three checked routes: compare the same label edit at two setups; reproduce and repair the billing defect; recover the unavailable sheet and verify today’s total.
A clear boundary can be useful. First identify whether something is missing, disallowed, or simply not requested.
The saved draft matches the approved source and remains unsent. You changed the relevant access boundary, connected the app separately, and checked the actual deliverable.
Read the approved source, connect the training mail app, save a draft and verify it. Use scoped filesystem access, leave unused command network access off, and resolve pending requests.
You can ask for the workspace you want. Let’s create a focused task with a clear outcome, then keep it easy to find.
The task has an outcome and a check. It can now work independently without mixing its result into an unrelated conversation.
Use a descriptive name, state what to produce, and include a concrete check or source comparison.
Pinning organizes the workspace. It does not change the model, context, or permissions.
Sidebar organization and model behavior are separate controls.
Conversation history and files are two different things. Choose the kind of separation your work actually needs.
A conversation fork lets you explore another direction from existing history.
Choose the separation you need: conversation history or files.
You kept competing files separate, compared their actual changes, and verified the chosen record after integration. The other attempt is still available.
Complete the working-file exercise: create worktrees, run and check both attempts, compare their changes, integrate a passing result, then verify the local record.
You don’t need to wait silently. The right follow-up can correct the current work or prepare what comes next.
The status request preserved the job. Your correction changed the active checklist, and the queued email used its checked French result. Both deliverables are saved and the draft is unsent.
Ask for status, apply the French correction during the checklist run, then finish a queued email based on the latest checked result. Empty the waiting queue before keeping the sequence.
A confident answer can still hide a quiet mistake. Let’s inspect the thing that will actually be used.
You reproduced the bad output, made line-specific repairs, inspected the final diff, and verified the saved code against three inputs. Your repair and runnable checks are in the toolkit.
Run acceptance checks to reproduce the defect, repair the flagged lines, rerun the checks, and inspect the final diff before keeping it.
Tools make actions possible. Skills preserve the way you want a job done. Plugins can bring those pieces together.
The read tool retrieved both briefs. Project guidance set the output rules, and the repaired skill preserved each client’s own values. Both CSV files are checked and saved in your toolkit.
Connect Source Kit to Training briefs, read the guidance, reproduce the first procedure’s defect, then run and check both clients with the reusable skill.
The screenshot looks fine. Now let’s find out whether the page works.
You observed the failure, changed the save behavior, and verified the persisted record against the source. That is evidence of a working repair.
Finish the whole check: reproduce the disappearing record, repair it, then save Nina Patel and reload. A success message alone is not evidence.
Functional evidence and visual assessment answer different questions. Both matter to the actual experience.
One successful path does not establish usability across states and layouts.
Before asking a workflow to repeat, make sure it works once. Then give the next run a clear job.

The schedule has a tested prompt, explicit local time and execution requirements. Your run history separates quiet success, actionable findings, read failures and an offline host. The tested schedule and reports are in your toolkit.

Use the tested weekday 09:00 Toronto setup in this task. Observe a quiet run, new missing approval, read failure, recovery and an offline host. Finish a successful scheduled run after restoring the host, and leave the schedule active.
The work is only finished when someone else can use it, understand its limits, and recover if something goes wrong.

You checked the actual delivery route, preserved and tested recovery, repaired the asset path and verified the current package. The exported page, CSV, brand asset and instructions are ready for independent inspection.

Preserve a checked recovery copy, observe the delivery failure and verify its rollback. Then use the relative asset path, include useful instructions, check locally, rebuild, stage and check the repaired delivery.
Cedar Research has a new reporting brief. I’ll step back. Choose the context and tools, inspect the saved result, and show that your procedure works when the inputs change.
Your saved report, second-period check and recurring rehearsal satisfy the five evidence dimensions. The exported files preserve your first submission and any hint use.
Review the missing evidence, repair the working files or configuration, then submit again. Your first submitted score stays in the record.
